title: Exclude arbitrary fixed-chart relays at nine rank-seven BIT deadlines
body:
**Arbitrary finite paid relay networks on the retained charts cannot improve the nine original rank-seven BIT arrivals into chart 0.** The original price `7^t` is minimum for every `0<t<=1`, with free retention, local XOR and access to all strictly earlier original stock. This permits new intermediate forms, branching, merging, cycles and cancellation. It extends [PR #7741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7741)'s direct-bundle result at these nine deadlines. **No new kappa** or relay guarantee at the other 5,733 arrivals is claimed.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/PROOF.md), [tree/path receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/RESULT.json), [verifier](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/verify.py), [exact source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bd2684e60d122e7c490f0b4fbceb97742584b773/research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor/CREDITS.md).

Every improving network must have total integer rank at most six. Its relevant chart component has a spanning tree within that budget. If a dimension-six chart occurs, the whole tree is a strictly increasing nested chain from zero to six. Otherwise its dimensions are 0, 1, 2 and 4. These cases bound the support of every form available to the receiver, even after new relay combinations.

| Complete necessary bound | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Low-dimensional trees: support at most 37 | Exact rooted-tree recurrence with arbitrary branching; an independent coarse cut bound also gives 42<48 |
| Chains reaching dimension six: support at most 35 | All 37,872 chains; exact source support unions |
| Separate path census | Forward and reverse constructions agree on all 40,667 increasing paths |
| Required arrivals: distance at least 48 | All 511 target-coset vectors in the unchanged predecessor certificate |
| Attained old price | The original source and nested rank-seven transfer remain feasible |

Thus every cheaper network has projected nonroot support at most **37**, while every required target representative has weight at least **48**. The old direct-only cap of 30 does fail on an actual relay chain; the new result charges and covers that changed information flow. The 37 bound is an upper bound for actual stock, not a claimed exact communication capacity.

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-nine-deadline-relay-floor
```

Both registered normal and optimized commands print:

```text
PASS_BIT_NINE_DEADLINE_RELAY_FLOOR all relays: support<=37<48
```

Normal/optimized registered replay, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay pass. The complete retained PR7741 verifier runs first, including its source geometry, two paid-row representations, all attainments, donor supports, cosets and controls. New controls cover the direct-only cap, false strict separation, support unions and charged extra branches. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44401302559/job/135144722957) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Ali Romman supplied the [fixed quotient and coset proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/PROOF.md) and [certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/RESULT.json). Nick Petalas supplied [PR #7739](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7739)'s reduction and nine exceptions. [PR #7723](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7723) supplied the fixed-library model, and Jerry Chen supplied the selected [PR #7001](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7001) caller. The [retained credit file](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e/research/bit-all-bundle-price-floor/CREDITS.md) preserves zxv, DreamingOfClouds, Cinna Davis and earlier native/root attribution. Their bytes and notices remain intact.

The model fixes charts, independent inputs, original stock, target rows and deadlines. New charts can change the obstruction: a proposed dimension-three hub with three dimension-four sources has rank bill `1+1+1+3=6`, but no compatible source intersection, target reconstruction or physical caller is supplied. The other 5,733 arrivals need their own relay analysis. All five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged. The selected cold replay, unrelated historical suites, Lean, Docker and physical relay execution were not run.

Base: canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, revision 8. The complete eighteen-file predecessor package is retained at `33817d65c801232f1e07355f43ec6040a41e7c7e`; its own eight source pins remain intact. No unmerged source ancestry is asserted. Geometry and source replay are shared code. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human or formal-kernel acceptance. Apache-2.0. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718575).
